decisive_items: atopic dermatitis treated with prednisone 80 mg daily for the past year
bilateral opacification of the sphenoid and ethmoid sinuses
left intraorbital involvement with contrast enhancement, and extension into the cavernous sinus causing pachymeningeal enhancement
response.rationale: Immunosuppression (chronic high-dose prednisone) plus progressive sino-orbital-cavernous involvement strongly favors invasive fungal sinusitis; other candidates lack the combination of risk factor and aggressive local extension.

rejected.why: GPA typically has more systemic and pulmonary involvement; no ANCA or necrotizing granulomas described.
Meningitis alone does not explain sinus opacification and orbital/cavernous extension.
Orbital cellulitis usually follows sinusitis but lacks the cavernous sinus and pachymeningeal extension and immunosuppressive context.
Tolosa-Hunt is idiopathic granulomatous inflammation, not associated with sinus opacification or immunosuppression.
Cushingoid appearance is a side effect of steroids, not the primary diagnosis explaining the acute orbital/sinus process.
Simple sinusitis does not explain intraorbital and cavernous sinus involvement.

Metastatic disease could cause orbital lesions but less likely to produce bilateral sinus opacification and cavernous extension without a known recurrence; fungal infection is more consistent with immunosuppression.
